record.paper_title: Some open problems concerning the convergence of positive series
record.context_brief: weighted-density criteria for divergent harmonic subseries
record.original_question: Let A be a subset of the positive integers. For an increasing function phi: N -> (0, infinity) with phi(n) -> infinity, define the phi-weighted upper density of A by dbar_phi(A) = limsup as n -> infinity of |A intersect [1, n]| / phi(n). If dbar_{n/log n}(A) > 0, must the harmonic subseries sum_{n in A} 1/n diverge? More generally, for weights phi(n) = n / ((log n)(log log n)...(the k-fold iterated logarithm of n)) when these iterated logarithms are defined, does positive phi-weighted upper density force sum_{n in A} 1/n to diverge?

evidence.quote: Problem 3. Given an increasing function ϕ : N →(0, ∞) with limn→∞ ϕ(n) = ∞, we define the upper density of weight ϕ by the formula d¯ϕ(A) = lim sup |A ∩ [1, n]| / ϕ(n).
Does every subset A ⊂ N with d¯n/ ln n (A) > 0 generate a divergent subseries ∑_{n∈A} 1/n of the harmonic series?
What about the case of other weights n/[(ln n) (ln ln n) · · · (ln · · · ln n)]?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a subset $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}=\{1,2,3,\dots\}$ and an increasing function $\varphi:\mathbb{N}\to(0,\infty)$ with $\lim_{n\to\infty}\varphi(n)=\infty$, define the upper density of $A$ with weight $\varphi$ by
$$\overline{d}_\varphi(A)=\limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{|A\cap[1,n]|}{\varphi(n)}.$$

(1) Suppose $\overline{d}_\varphi(A)>0$ for the weight $\varphi(n)=n/\ln n$ (defined for $n\ge 2$). Must the subseries $\sum_{n\in A}\frac{1}{n}$ of the harmonic series diverge?

(2) More generally, for each integer $k\ge 1$ let
$$\varphi_k(n)=\frac{n}{(\ln n)(\ln\ln n)\cdots(\underbrace{\ln\cdots\ln}_{k\text{ times}}n)}$$
on the domain where the $k$-fold iterated logarithm is defined and positive. If $\overline{d}_{\varphi_k}(A)>0$, must $\sum_{n\in A}\frac{1}{n}$ diverge?

Determine whether each implication holds, or exhibit a counterexample.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search located the problem list where this question is posed, as well as classical work of Powell and Šalát on convergence of harmonic subseries via asymptotic density (which gives only that r-convergence implies density zero, not the converse direction at the finer scale $n/\log n$). No source was found that explicitly resolves the $n/\ln n$-weighted density question or its iterated-logarithm generalization, so the current status appears to be open/unknown based on available evidence.

status_evidence.snippet: Studies relationship between asymptotic density and convergence of harmonic subseries.
status_evidence.claim: Related classical work addresses density vs. r-convergence but not the finer weight $n/\log n$.

status_evidence.title: On Convergent Subseries of the Harmonic Series
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses r-convergent sets and density 0; primes are r-divergent with density 0.
status_evidence.claim: No converse implication at density-zero scale is proved; the $n/\log n$-weight version is not resolved here.
